rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: The formula of washing soda is
rows.solution:
Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate: each formula unit of sodium carbonate carries ten molecules of water of crystallisation. (\(\mathrm{NaHCO_3}\) is baking soda, which has no water of crystallisation.)

This is option (D) \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\).

rows.stem: The nature of aqueous solution of potassium nitrate is :
rows.solution:
Potassium nitrate is the salt of a strong acid (nitric acid) and a strong base (potassium hydroxide), so its aqueous solution is neutral, with pH 7.

This is option (C) neutral.

options.text: cross pollinating \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation plants with plants having dominant trait.

options.label: C
options.text: cross pollinating \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation plants with plants having recessive trait.

rows.solution:
Mendel first crossed the two pure parent plants to get the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation. He then allowed the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants to self-pollinate, and the seeds so produced gave the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation.

This is option (A) self pollinating \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation plants.

rows.stem: When a seed germinates the root grows downwards and a small shoot grows upward. This shoot is known as
rows.solution:
In a germinating seed the embryo has two parts: the radicle, which grows down into the root, and the plumule, which grows up into the shoot. The cotyledons store food for the growing embryo.

This is option (D) plumule.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Most of the refraction for the light rays entering the eye occurs at
rows.solution:
Light entering the eye is refracted mostly at the outer surface of the cornea, where it passes from air into the cornea and the change in optical density is the largest. The crystalline lens only fine-tunes the focus, and the iris and pupil control the amount of light.

This is option (D) Outer surface of Cornea.

rows.stem: Green plants occupy the first trophic level in every food chain because they

options.label: B
options.text: have very less concentration of harmful chemicals.

options.label: C
options.text: have to feed large number of herbivores.

rows.solution:
Green plants (producers) make their own food from sunlight, carbon dioxide and water by photosynthesis. Every other organism depends on this food, directly or indirectly, so the producers always form the first trophic level.

This is option (D) can synthesize food by photosynthesis.

rows.stem:
Cinnabar is an ore of a metal ‘X’. When this ore is heated in air, it is first converted into oxide of ‘X’ (XO) and then reduced to metal ‘X’ on further heating.

Identify metal ‘X’ and write chemical equations for the reactions that occur in the above processes.
rows.solution:
Cinnabar (\(\mathrm{HgS}\)) is an ore of mercury, so 'X' is mercury (Hg).

When cinnabar is heated in air, it is first converted into mercuric oxide:

\(\mathrm{2HgS(s) + 3O_2(g) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2HgO(s) + 2SO_2(g)}\)

On further heating, mercuric oxide is reduced to mercury:

\(\mathrm{2HgO(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2Hg(l) + O_2(g)}\)

rows.stem: Indicate the flow of energy in a food chain operating in an ecosystem. Why is it uni-directional ? Give reason.
rows.solution:
Energy flows in one direction along the food chain:

\(\text{Sun} \rightarrow \text{Producers (green plants)} \rightarrow \text{Herbivores} \rightarrow \text{Carnivores}\)

It is uni-directional because the energy captured by the autotrophs does not go back to the solar input, and the energy that passes to the herbivores does not come back to the autotrophs. At each level part of the energy is also lost as heat, so it moves progressively from one trophic level to the next and never reverts.

rows.stem:
In an experiment a student dipped pH papers in four different solutions A, B, C and D and reported his observation as given below :

| **Solution** | A | B | C | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Colour of pH paper** | Light green | Blue | Green | Red |

(i) In which one of these solutions is the concentration of (1) hydrogen / hydronium ions; (2) hydroxyl ions maximum ?

(ii) Give one example each of the two solutions identified in (i) above.

(iii) What would be the pH of the resultant mixture obtained when these two solutions are mixed together in equal proportions ? Justify your answer.
rows.solution:
(i) Red pH paper means a strongly acidic solution and blue means a strongly basic one.

(1) The concentration of hydrogen (hydronium) ions is maximum in solution D.

(2) The concentration of hydroxyl ions is maximum in solution B.

(ii) Solution D: a strong acid such as hydrochloric acid (HCl), sulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)) or nitric acid (\(\mathrm{HNO_3}\)). Solution B: a strong base such as sodium hydroxide (NaOH) or potassium hydroxide (KOH).

(iii) When a strong acid and a strong base are mixed in equal proportions, the resulting solution has a pH of 7: it is neutral. The acid and the base neutralise each other completely, forming salt and water and leaving no excess hydrogen or hydroxide ions:

\(\mathrm{HCl + NaOH \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(i) Name the gas liberated when an acid reacts with a metal. How is this gas tested ?

(ii) Write the chemical equation for the reaction of zinc metal with

(1) hydrochloric acid, and

(2) sodium hydroxide

Name the compound of zinc obtained in each case.
rows.solution:
(i) The gas liberated is hydrogen. It is tested by bringing a burning candle or matchstick near it: the gas burns with a pop sound.

(ii) (1) Zinc and hydrochloric acid:

\(\mathrm{Zn + 2HCl \rightarrow ZnCl_2 + H_2}\)

The compound of zinc formed is zinc chloride.

(2) Zinc and sodium hydroxide (on heating):

\(\mathrm{Zn + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2}\)

The compound of zinc formed is sodium zincate.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: An object of size 5 cm is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the optical centre of a converging lens of focal length 20 cm. Use lens formula to determine the position and size of the image formed.
rows.solution:
For a converging (convex) lens, \(f = +20\) cm, the object distance \(u = -30\) cm and the object height \(h_o = +5\) cm.

Position: by the lens formula,

\(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{20}\)

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{60} = \dfrac{1}{60}\), so \(v = +60\) cm.

The image is formed 60 cm from the lens, on the other side of the lens.

Size: the magnification is

\(m = \dfrac{h_i}{h_o} = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{60}{-30} = -2\)

so \(h_i = -2 \times 5 = -10\) cm.

The image is 10 cm high: real, inverted and enlarged (twice the size of the object).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
(a) Draw a diagram to show the dispersion of white light by a glass prism.

(b) What is spectrum ? Give reason for its formation.
rows.solution:
(a) Diagram: draw a triangular glass prism with a ray of white light falling obliquely on one face. Inside the prism the light splits into its colours, and on leaving the other face the colours spread out into a band, with red deviated the least (at the top) and violet the most (at the bottom). Label the white light beam, the glass prism and the spectrum (R to V).

(b) The band of seven colours obtained on a screen when white light is dispersed by a prism is called a spectrum (VIBGYOR: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red).

It forms because the different colours of white light bend through different angles with respect to the incident ray as they pass through the prism. Red bends the least and violet the most, so the colours separate.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem:
(a) Study the following electric circuit diagram and answer the questions that follow :

(i) What does the circuit diagram shows ?

(ii) What will happen if the direction of current is reversed ? Justify your answer giving circuit diagram.

(b) Name and state the rule to determine the direction of magnetic field associated with a straight current carrying conductor.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - part (a) is posed on a printed circuit: a closed loop with a battery, a plug key K and current arrows, a magnetic compass placed beside one straight segment of the wire with its N and S ends marked, and a compass-direction rose with a curved arrow showing which way the needle turns. What the diagram demonstrates and the direction of the deflection are withheld here. Page idx 24.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) The circuit shows the magnetic effect of electric current: the compass needle placed near the current-carrying straight wire is deflected (here towards the east). So an electric current through a conductor produces a magnetic field around it.

(ii) If the direction of the current is reversed, the compass needle deflects in the opposite direction (towards the west). Reversing the current reverses the direction of the magnetic field around the wire, and the needle always lines up with the field.

Circuit diagram: draw the same circuit with the cell reversed (or with the current arrows reversed), the plug key K closed and the compass beside the same straight segment of wire, with the needle now deflected the other way, towards the west.

(b) The rule is the right-hand thumb rule. Imagine that you are holding the current-carrying straight conductor in your right hand so that the thumb points in the direction of the current. Then the fingers wrap around the conductor in the direction of the field lines of the magnetic field.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem:
(a) Draw the pattern of magnetic field lines of

(i) a bar magnet

(ii) a current carrying solenoid

List two distinguishing features between the two magnetic fields.

(b) Study the following three diagrams in which the entry of an electron in a magnetic field is shown. Identify the case in which the magnetic force experienced by the electron is (i) maximum, and (ii) minimum.

Give reason for your answers in each case.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - part (b) is posed on three printed diagrams labelled (A), (B) and (C), each showing an electron's path entering a region of parallel magnetic field lines; the angle between the electron's path and the field in each case is the whole of what the question tests, so it is withheld here. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) Bar magnet: the field lines are closed curves that come out of the north pole, curve round outside the magnet and enter the south pole; inside the magnet they run from the south pole to the north pole. They are crowded near the poles, where the field is strongest, and never cross. Mark arrows on the lines from N to S outside the magnet.

(ii) Current-carrying solenoid: draw a coil of many turns connected to a cell and a key. Inside the solenoid the field lines are parallel straight lines along its axis; outside they curve round from one end to the other, just like those of a bar magnet, so one end behaves as a north pole and the other as a south pole.

Two distinguishing features:

The strength of the magnetic field of a bar magnet is fixed; that of a solenoid can be changed (by changing the current or the number of turns).

The polarity of a bar magnet is fixed; the polarity of a solenoid can be changed by reversing the direction of the current.

(b) The force on a moving charge in a magnetic field is largest when it moves at right angles to the field, and zero when it moves along the field (in the same or the opposite direction).

(i) The force is maximum in case (A), because the electron moves perpendicular to the magnetic field.

(ii) The force is minimum (zero) in case (C), because the electron moves along the field line, in the direction opposite to the magnetic field. In case (B) the electron enters at an angle, so the force lies between these two.
